title: Missing error boundaries for route components
reasoning: The application defines 30+ routes but has no React error boundary wrapping the router or individual routes. If any route component throws an unhandled error during rendering, the entire application will crash and display a blank screen. This is particularly risky given the large number of portal components (Portal, BundleChat, MarkPortal, BrianPortal, etc.) that likely make API calls or handle dynamic data.
reproduction: Navigate to any route that throws an error during render (e.g., a portal component that fails to fetch data). The entire app will unmount and show a white screen instead of a user-friendly error message.
recommendation: Wrap the <BrowserRouter> or <Routes> component with a React ErrorBoundary component that catches rendering errors and displays a fallback UI. Consider per-route error boundaries for critical routes to isolate failures.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included in this feature (tests array is empty), so there's no coverage for error handling scenarios or component error recovery.
suggestedRegressionTest: Create an integration test that: 1) Simulates a component error in one of the route handlers, 2) Verifies that an error boundary catches it, 3) Asserts a fallback UI is displayed instead of a crash.
minimumFixScope: src/src/main.tsx - wrap Routes with ErrorBoundary component
